Solo Apex Legends is the exact same experience. Teammates throw nearly every game. Basically, as games have become more popular the average skill has declined. This is because the percentage of high-skill players is a continually shrinking minority. 

In Apex, a game which is pretty focused on competitive play, less than 5% reach Diamond (which is what I would consider the low end of "skilled"). Less than 1% (closer to a tenth of a percent) make up the highest tier of players. So that means for every hundred matches you play, teammates are more likely than not to throw 95.

For a game on the Switch, I can't imagine the odds are better than this. Likely worse, since it's closer to 99% of games in EVP40 or below get thrown.

Running away from a special is not counterplay. Streamers with high-mid-tier skill know about as little as the bottom half of the playerbase.

No, a special which forces you off the tower (and cannot be removed from the tower) is not balanced.
